name: Meeting Agenda
one_liner: The points to be discussed, timed and owned, sent out before the meeting — not improvised in the room.
purpose: The Meeting Agenda is the PM² template used to plan and run project meetings effectively. The guide's Planning Kick-off steps require the Project Manager to plan the meeting, draft an agenda clearly indicating the points to be discussed, send it out in advance, ensure the required participants attend, and prepare documentation and hand-outs. It records the meeting's identification, invited participants, objectives, timed agenda items with owners, and the documents participants must read beforehand.
created_in: Any phase — before every project meeting
approved_by: Not approved — issued by the Meeting Coordinator (the chairperson named in the Communications Management Plan)
inputs: Communications Management Plan (standing agenda items per meeting type)
Business Case and Project Charter (for the Planning Kick-off)
Project Handbook and Project Work Plan (for the Executing Kick-off)
Previous Minutes of Meeting — proposed agenda for next meeting
feeds: Project Handbook (via the Planning Kick-off MoM)
gate: None — supports every meeting, in every phase

lifecycle.what: Used for the Initiating Meeting and Charter workshops
Planning Kick-off agenda, issued in advance to all invited
Executing Kick-off, Status, PCT, Change Control agendas
Review and Steering Committee agendas driven by the plan

items: Free-text block — what must be true when the meeting ends
Taken from the meeting's Purpose row in the Communications Management Plan

fields.what: The name of the meeting, matching a meeting type defined in the Communications Management Plan so its standing purpose, attendees and media are already agreed.
Date and start/end time. Enough notice must be given for the agenda to be sent in advance and required participants to attend.
Which of the plan's meeting types this is — Planning Kick-off, Executing Kick-off, Status, PCT, Review, Steering Committee, Change Control, Project-End Review.
fields.castor: Planning Kick-off Meeting — held once at project level, per the Communications Management Plan.

fields.what: Where the meeting takes place, including remote joining arrangements; kick-off locations are defined by the PM in time.
fields.castor: ESM, Luxembourg City (Kirchberg), room B-2.04, with video for remote participants.

fields.what: The person organising and normally chairing the meeting. For the Planning Kick-off this is the Project Manager; for the PSC Meeting it would be the Project Owner.
fields.who: Per the Communications Management Plan chairperson row
fields.castor: Project Manager, ESM Project Support Office — the PM organises the Planning Kick-off.

fields.what: When the agenda was issued. The guide requires the agenda to be sent out in advance, so this date must clearly precede the meeting date.
fields.castor: 02 Apr 2026 — one week before the meeting, with the Charter attached.

fields.what: Everyone invited, by name. For the Planning Kick-off the required participants are PM, PCT, BIG, URs, SP, PO and BM; PMA and PSO attend if part of the project.
fields.who: Meeting Coordinator invites from the Stakeholder Matrix
fields.castor: Florence Nightingale, Leonardo da Vinci, Grace Hopper, Nikola Tesla, Ada Lovelace, Marie Curie, Henry Gantt.

fields.what: Short code for each participant, reused in the Minutes of Meeting to assign decision owners and action owners without repeating full names.
fields.castor: ÉM · RT · KB · JW · AO · AF · NR — carried through into the MoM action table.

fields.what: Contact details and home organisation of each invitee, which matter when contractors and other organisations attend; the master list stays in the Stakeholder Matrix.
fields.who: Taken from the Project Stakeholder Matrix
fields.castor: ESM Lending Operations, IT & Digital, Project Support Office; Levallois Systems not yet contracted.

fields.what: What the meeting must achieve. For the Planning Kick-off: everyone understands the scope, expectations of key stakeholders are clarified, risks are identified and the project plans are discussed.
fields.castor: Agree CASTOR scope and governance, set role expectations, and capture the first risk set before planning starts.

fields.what: The points to be discussed, clearly indicated. The Communications Management Plan holds the standing item list for each meeting type; the agenda instantiates it for this date.
fields.who: Meeting Coordinator drafts · PO contributes for kick-offs
fields.castor: Charter walkthrough, Planning Phase goals, governance and roles, timeline, approach, plans, risks, next steps.

fields.what: Time box per item. Timing forces the agenda to be realistic and protects the closing items — summary of decisions, actions and risks, and next steps.
fields.castor: 15 minutes for introductions, 30 for the Charter, 30 for risks, 15 to summarise and close.

fields.what: Who leads each item. Not everything belongs to the chair: the PO explains why the project matters, the SP speaks to approach, the PSO to supporting tools.
fields.castor: Florence Nightingale owns the business-importance item; Leonardo da Vinci the approach; Henry Gantt the tooling.

fields.what: The documents participants must read before the meeting, and where to find them — hand-outs and documentation the guide asks to be prepared beforehand.
fields.castor: 02.Business_Case and 03.Project_Charter (approved 24 Mar 2026), in 01 Initiating of the CASTOR repository.

traps: The agenda must be sent out in advance — that is an explicit guide step, not politeness.
PM² gives no RASCI row for the Meeting Agenda; the meeting has one, the artefact does not.
'Meeting Coordinator' here equals the 'Chairperson' row of the Communications Management Plan.
Planning Kick-off is chaired by the PM (RASCI PSC=A, PM=R); the PSC Meeting is chaired by the PO.
The agenda lists who was invited; only the MoM records who was actually Present.
